title: NORMAL_USER with no project membership is denied on a project-scoped route end-to-end through the full middleware chain
description: Exercises authenticate.js -> loadPermissions.js -> requirePermission.js together. Since CUSTOMER_BASELINE_PERMISSIONS is [] (loadPermissions.js:44) and the NORMAL_USER system role holds zero permissions (systemRoles.js), a user with no ProjectMember row anywhere must be denied on every project-scoped module.
preconditions: User has zero ProjectMember documents in any project
Valid RS256 JWT for this user
steps: Authenticate as the NORMAL_USER with a valid JWT
expectedResult: 403 Forbidden — 'Missing permission: evidence.read'. req.permissions resolved to an empty Set; no baseline or role permission granted evidence.read.

title: augmentPermissionsWithProjectGrant unlocks project-scoped permissions only for the specific project a user is a member of
description: middleware/augmentPermissionsWithProjectGrant.js:76-117. A live ProjectMember.findOne query (org+user+project scoped) folds the resolved ProjectRole permissions into req.permissions before requirePermission() runs, but only for the projectId resolved from the current request.
preconditions: User U is a ProjectMember (Project Member role) of Project A only
Project B exists in the same organization
steps: As User U, call GET /api/evidence?projectId=<Project A id>
As User U, call GET /api/evidence?projectId=<Project B id>
expectedResult: The Project A call succeeds (200, evidence.read folded in from the Project Member role). The Project B call is denied 403 — no ProjectMember row exists there, so no permissions are augmented for that project.

title: First login of a Keycloak-invited user with no MongoDB record JIT-creates a NORMAL_USER with zero effective permissions
description: loadPermissions.js:257-263 and jitCreateUser (317-387). When an admin invites a user directly from the Keycloak console (bypassing the app), the first authenticated request creates a User document with the NORMAL_USER system role, which resolves to req.permissions = empty Set until they're added to a project.
preconditions: A Keycloak user exists with no matching MongoDB User document (no keycloakUserId link, no invited-by-email record)
steps: Log in as the Keycloak-only user for the first time
Inspect the newly created MongoDB User document
Call GET /api/client/users/me and inspect the permissions array
expectedResult: A new User document is created with roleIds pointing at the NORMAL_USER system role, status='active'. GET /users/me returns an empty (or near-empty) permissions array — no operational access until added to a project.

title: Redis authz cache round-trips the resolved permission set and roleKeys correctly
description: loadPermissions.js:174-188 (read) and 298-299 (write via setAuthzCache, fire-and-forget). Confirms the cached shape ({permissions, roleKeys}) is read back into an identical Set + userRoles array on the next request, including baseline re-injection for organizations of the relevant kind.
preconditions: User with a known role/permission set logs in for the first time this session (cache miss)
steps: Make an authenticated request that triggers a DB-backed permission resolution and populates the Redis cache key authz:{orgId}:{userId}
Make a second authenticated request immediately after
Inspect req.permissions and req.userRoles on both requests
expectedResult: Both requests resolve to the identical effective permission set. The second request's timing/DB query count shows it served from Redis (no second Mongo populate query), confirming the cache round-trip is correct.

title: Admin-portal claim short-circuits organization resolution and enforcePortalBoundary entirely
description: loadPermissions.js:133-143 checks req.kcResourceAccess['admin-portal'] BEFORE any organization/kind lookup, setting req.isAdminPortal=true and req.permissions=generateFullAccess(). portalBoundary.js:35 then no-ops for isAdminPortal===true regardless of organizationKind.
preconditions: A verified Keycloak JWT whose resource_access includes 'admin-portal'
steps: Authenticate with an admin-portal JWT that also happens to carry a stale/unrelated organization claim
Call an ordinary customer-scoped route, e.g. GET /api/evidence
expectedResult: Request succeeds with full generateFullAccess() permissions; req.organizationKind/req.portalMode are never resolved for this request, and enforcePortalBoundary's MSSP/customer path split is bypassed entirely (by design for platform admins).

title: Saving a Custom org Role containing a project-scoped permission is rejected end-to-end
description: utils/catalogSeparation.js's assertNoProjectScopedInOrgGrant, invoked from role.controller.js on Role create/update. With CATALOG_SEPARATION_ENFORCEMENT defaulting to 'enforce' (2026-07-22), submitting a project-scoped permission string (e.g. 'evidence.create') into a Custom Role's permissions array must fail the write.
preconditions: Logged in as an org admin (role.create permission)
expectedResult: 400 Bad Request: 'These permissions are not allowed here: evidence.create'. The Role document is not created/updated. A security-classified warn log (authz.catalog_separation.violation) is emitted.

title: An mssp_provider-kind organization's user is denied on a customer-only route even with valid auth and permissions
description: portalBoundary.js:38-43 (enforcePortalBoundary) plus loadPermissions.js:163-170 (active MsspProvider status check) run in sequence for every request. A provider user with mssp_dashboard.read cannot reach /api/evidence — only paths in MSSP_ALLOWED_PREFIXES (/api/auth/, /api/mssp, /api/bug-reports, /api/contact) are reachable.
preconditions: User authenticated with a valid JWT for this organization
steps: As the mssp_provider user, call GET /api/mssp/clients (allowed prefix) — expect success
As the same user, call GET /api/evidence (customer-only route)
expectedResult: The /api/mssp/clients call succeeds. The /api/evidence call is rejected with 403 PORTAL_BOUNDARY_DENIED ('This account cannot access the requested workspace'), independent of whatever permissions the provider role holds.
